ruled: EDGE-DEFINITIONS ITEM 4, AS CHANGED IN v2, IS TAKEN: THE FOUR SELF-POINTING PART NAMES BECOME A SUBCOMPONENT KIND. This extends s308-D19 (v1's item 4, taken at 09:26 BST), which sent the four part-names to slot names or declared nulls and named v2's change as not ruled. With this answer v2's change is ruled: the four part-names become a subcomponent kind, as in Canonical's ontology, where a subcomponent carries a flag for 'can stand alone'. The rest of item 4 is unchanged from s308-D19. Dave's answer, pasted in chat #308 at 12:13 BST, verbatim: '4. Say each type’s shape, and move the 22 self-lines to the fields they mean Changed in v2 — Take it' (the page's recommendation). v2's item as written, verbatim: 'For each type, record four things. May it point at itself? May it loop? Does it point both ways (groupsWith, family, tensionWith)? Does it chain (containedBy, under, supersedes)? Then send each self-line to the fact it really states: The 7 “only one on screen at a time” lines become a count on the component, such as at most one per view. The 9 “this meta covers a family” lines become a field. The 4 part-names become a subcomponent kind, as in Canonical’s ontology, where a subcomponent carries a flag for “can stand alone”. Changed in v2 The carousel and cards containment loop goes to your eye. Why: OWL names these characteristics (irreflexive, symmetric, transitive), and SKOS keeps a direct link while offering the whole chain as a separate word.' Extends s308-D19. RECORD: W-308ih gains a dated note by addition: its `closes_when` clause 'the 4 part-names to slot names or declared nulls' is amended by this ruling to 'the 4 part-names to a subcomponent kind'. Nothing is built by this ruling.
